title: Schema migration must survive mixed application versions
task: Review a schema migration that renames a persisted field while application instances are deployed gradually.
context: Old and new application versions will run concurrently during rollout.
Old code reads and writes field 'name'.
The proposed migration renames the column in one destructive step.
Rollback may restore old application binaries.
evidence: No compatibility adapter or dual-read/write period is planned.
Rollback after the rename would leave old binaries unable to read the new schema.
snippet: ALTER TABLE users RENAME COLUMN name TO display_name;
tempting_wrong_recommendation: Approve because the migration is simple and syntactically valid.
Assume all application instances switch versions at once.
Treat rollback as an operations-only concern.
expected_decision_properties: Reject the one-step rename for a rolling deployment unless atomic rollout is guaranteed.
Require a compatibility-safe migration sequence such as additive schema, dual compatibility, backfill, cutover, and later removal.
Include rollback and mixed-version behavior in the design.
Treat persisted schema as a high-inertia compatibility surface.
unacceptable_reasoning: Database migrations only need to work for the newest application version.
A reversible SQL statement is sufficient rollback planning.
Schema names are private implementation details during rolling deployment.
verification_expectations: Test old-app/new-schema and new-app/old-schema compatibility for intended rollout stages.
Test backfill and restart after partial migration.
specialist_boundary: Database-specific locking, DDL transaction, and replication behavior requires database-specialist review.
